chunks: We were told by Abu’l-Hasan, Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Asad al-Asadi, that he said: We were told by Muhammad ibn Jarir, and Hasan ibn ‘Urwa, and Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Wahbi, that they said: We were told by Muhammad ibn Hameed, that he said: We were told by Zafir ibn Sulayman, that he said: We were told by Muhammad ibn ‘Uyayna, from Abu Hazem, from Sahl ibn Sa’eed, that he said: Jibra’eel, peace be upon him, came to the Prophet, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, and said: O Muhammad, live however you want, for indeed, you are to die, and love what you want, for indeed, you are to separate from it, and do what you want, for indeed, you are to be rewarded for it. Moreover, know that the honor of a man is his standing during the night, and his honor is his sufficiency from people.

key_terms.قِيَامُهُ بِاللَّيْلِ: His standing in prayer during the night (night prayer)
key_terms.مُجْزَى بِهِ: He will be rewarded for it

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of a man's honor and dignity according to the hadith of Jibra’il?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, this hadith presents a concise cosmology of the human condition, reminding the believer of mortality, separation, and accountability to motivate spiritual diligence. It redefines nobility not by lineage or wealth, but through *Qiyam al-Layl* (night prayer) and *Istighna* (self-sufficiency), reflecting the Shia emphasis on inner piety and detachment from worldly dependence as markers of true status.
